I've been farming this land in Quzhou for most of my life. My father farmed it before me, and his father before him. The soil here on the North China Plain is deep and flat — good for grain. I know what works.

There's really only one system that makes sense here: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. Everyone does it. The wheat goes in around October 1st after we've tilled, and comes out in June. Then we put the maize in right away — no time to waste — and pull it out in late September. Two crops a year, same 8 mu.

For wheat, I use an improved variety — Jimai 22 or whatever the seed station is selling this autumn. Not the fanciest stuff, but reliable. I put down compound fertilizer as a base before sowing, then top-dress with urea at jointing. Water four times: at sowing, before winter freezes in, at jointing, and again at heading. The aquifer has been dropping — my neighbor complains about it — but I don't know another way. Spray herbicide in late winter, spray fungicide near heading to fight rust. Rotary till the corn stubble under before planting.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed — Xianyu 335, same as the past few years, good yield. I direct-seed right into the wheat stubble without tilling, saves time and my back at my age. Fertilize once at sowing, top-dress at the big bell stage. Maize usually catches the summer rains but I irrigate twice to be safe. One pesticide pass for stem borer.

I'm 64. My sons are in the city. I manage this myself and with my wife helping at busy times. I keep it simple and I know what I'm doing.
